chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Walking 52nd Street with Joe Glaser, Winchell and Ed Sullivan
summary: McRae became friends with Glaser, strolling to Cafe Society with Jack Robbins, Walter Winchell and Ed Sullivan.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts

blocks.x: After that -- now this is what leads up to the Louie Armstrong thing. After I had worked with Joe Glaser on the Street and did such a great job down there, he wanted --
He and I became real good friends then, you know. I used to meet him and we to go walk with -- Ed Sullivan (inaudible).
Here would be the (inaudible). Listen to this. Joe would call me up and ask me what I'm doing I say "You wanna walk with me?"
I say, "I'll meet you." We would meet at 52nd Street -- 53rd Street around Ed Sullivan Theater.. The theater, see, must be an office in there.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
He'd come out and Ed would come out with Joe Glaser, Walter Winchell. And this -- we gonna do the street. We're going on 52nd Street. Walter Winchell would be -- and myself.
Now I don't know why Joe called me up. "Come on and walk with me." So I meet him. We come down to 53rd Street.
We pick up Walter Winchell. Walter Winchell would be some place else. We go by and pick him up.
And Ed Sullivan would come out of the now here come -- theater and (inaudible). And we go on 52nd Street, we go some place else.
One time we go down to the Village, you know. Walter Winchell would be going around getting his sheet together.
He had a lot of ghost writers out there too. He be walking around finding out what's going on, you know.
He be going around and getting his column and stuff together. And we be walking around
